## Fatal findings

1. `thm-a-complete-locally-small-category-with-a-jointly-weakly-initial-set-has-an-initial-object` — [proof step 3.1](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-a-complete-locally-small-category-with-a-jointly-weakly-initial-set-has-an-initial-object.md:56)

   The inference from “$p_Sr$ and $p_S$ are cones” to $p_Sr=p_S$ is invalid. [L4’s dependency](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-limit-and-colimit-of-a-diagram.md:27) gives a unique mediator for each fixed cone; it does not identify two different cones. The reasoning is circular: $r$ is a cone endomorphism only after $p_Sr=p_S$ has already been established.

   Concrete witness to the invoked rule: in `Set`, take the one-object identity diagram at $X=\{0,1\}$. Its limit cone is $(X,1_X)$, but for a nonidentity endomorphism $r:X\to X$, both $1_X$ and $r$ are cone legs from apex $X$, and they are unequal.

   Thus $r=1_L$, invertibility of the equalizer, and uniqueness of maps $L\to C$ are not proved. This also removes the local proof backbone of the objectwise GAFT and Freyd representability items that cite this theorem. **Severity: fatal.**

2. `cor-functor-categories-inherit-completeness-and-cocompleteness` — direct dependency, [title](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/cor-functor-categories-inherit-completeness-and-cocompleteness.md:4)

   The title asserts completeness/cocompleteness of $[\mathcal A,\mathcal C]$ from smallness of $\mathcal A$ and completeness/cocompleteness of $\mathcal C$, without Choice. The [Statement](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/cor-functor-categories-inherit-completeness-and-cocompleteness.md:28) begins “Assume Choice,” and step 1.1 uses Choice to select the pointwise limits simultaneously. The title therefore asserts more than the proof delivers. **Severity: fatal.**

3. `cor-a-continuous-functor-to-set-from-a-chosen-well-powered-saft-category-is-representable` — [title](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/cor-a-continuous-functor-to-set-from-a-chosen-well-powered-saft-category-is-representable.md:4)

   The title promises representability from the chosen-well-powered SAFT hypotheses alone. The [Statement](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/cor-a-continuous-functor-to-set-from-a-chosen-well-powered-saft-category-is-representable.md:26) additionally assumes a supplied family of objectwise universal arrows, and [proof step 1.1](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/cor-a-continuous-functor-to-set-from-a-chosen-well-powered-saft-category-is-representable.md:42) explicitly uses that family to assemble a left adjoint.

   “Supplied well-powering” does not include those universal-arrow choices: its [definition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-well-powered-and-co-well-powered-category.md:29) supplies only subobject representatives. Hence the proof does not deliver the title’s no-universal-family formulation. **Severity: fatal.**

## Nonfatal findings

4. `cor-a-complete-locally-small-category-with-a-small-coseparating-set-and-saft-intersections-is-cocomplete` — [proof step 1.1](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/cor-a-complete-locally-small-category-with-a-small-coseparating-set-and-saft-intersections-is-cocomplete.md:48) and the contract’s `nonempty-choice` boundary

   Step 1.1 invokes [L5], whose cited [Statement explicitly assumes Choice](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/cor-functor-categories-inherit-completeness-and-cocompleteness.md:28), but the assigned corollary does not assume Choice. Its [contract row](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/frontier-14-batch-6.proof-contracts.json:2316) also falsely says the authored proof makes no such selection.

   This is nonfatal under the 30-second rule: continuity of the diagonal can be shown directly—if $L=\lim E$ in $\mathcal C$, then $\Delta L$ with the constant limiting cone is pointwise the limit of $\Delta E$—without choosing unrelated pointwise limits. **Severity: nonfatal.**

5. `thm-freyd-representability-theorem` — proof-contract `one` boundary

   The [contract row](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/frontier-14-batch-6.proof-contracts.json:2541) says no singleton or one-valued parameter occurs. But [proof step 2.1](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-freyd-representability-theorem.md:50) explicitly identifies $\int F$ with $(1\downarrow F)$ “for a singleton $1$.” The proof handles the singleton correctly; only the boundary disposition is false. **Severity: nonfatal.**
